question.leadin: This ruler founded the Achaemenid [ah-KEE-men-id] Empire, which successfully grew by supporting local rulers as satraps and respecting local customs.
question.text: Name this "Great" Persian ruler of the sixth century BCE who ended the Babylonian Captivity.
question.clue: This man's Edict of Restoration established a policy of religious tolerance in his empire, and as a result, is the only non-Jew in the Tanakh to be named a Messiah.

swap.leadin: At the Battles of Issus and Gaugamela, Alexander the Great defeated forces from this empire.
swap.text: Name this empire, which was ruled for some periods by Achaemenids, Safavids, and Afshars. Rulers of this empire included Cyrus the Great and Xerxes (ZERK-seez) the Great.
swap.clue: According to the Demotic Chronicle, this empire was responsible for smashing many temples to Egyptian gods.

question.leadin: Answer some questions about the SAVAK secret police force.
question.text: SAVAK was active in this country until its 1979 revolution, which saw the overthrow of its Shah Mohammad Reza Pahlavi. More than 50 Americans were held hostage in this country's city of Tehran.
question.answerHtml: Iran [or Islamic Republic of Iran or Jomhuri-ye Eslami-ye Iran; accept Iranian Revolution]
question.clue: This country has the 2nd largest gas reserves in the world, and is the 4th largest producer of petroleum.

swap.leadin: Give the following related to first Persian invasion of Greece.
swap.text: This "Great" Persian leader, who avenged the death of Cyrus the Great by attacking Scythia, invaded Greece after the Ionian Revolt.
swap.clue: After his predecessor died of gangrene, this king and six other nobles assassinated a magician pretending to be Bardiya named Gaumata, an event described in his cliff-face Behistun Inscription.

question.leadin: This victor of the battles of Ipsus and Corupedium was succeeded in his highest post by his son Antiochus after his assassination.
question.text: Name this Diadochos who established a namesake empire in the former easternmost satrapies of Alexander the Great.
question.clue: He dispatched the ambassador Megasthenes on expeditions to the east, resulting in the production of theIndika.

swap.leadin: Translations of the Hebrew Bible into this language were known as targum.
swap.text: Name this ancient Semitic language, used as a lingua franca in Mesopotamia and Judea. Jesus Christ spoke this language inscribed on the sarcophagus of Eshmunazar II.
swap.clue: Demons found in the Ginza Rabba were repelled using ceramic bowls with incantations in this language.

question.text: After Roman triumvirate Crassus tried to invade this empire and failed, his was head was cut off and filled with molten gold in reference to his famous wealth.
question.clue: A train of camels bearing arrows helped this state win a major victory, after which its forces poured molten gold down an invading general's throat.

swap.leadin: Answer some questions about the life of the Byzantine emperor Justinian in 532 A.D.
swap.text: In September 532, Justinian signed an "Eternal Peace" with Khosrau I, a king of this empire. Another ruler of this empire captured the Roman emperor Valerian after the Battle of Edessa.
swap.clue: This empire was defeated at Qadisiyyah at the hands of Umar's general, Khalid ibn al-Walid.

question.leadin: The Hall of Hundred Columns in this city has the same dimensions as Athens's Odeon.
question.text: Identify this ceremonial capital in the Zagros Mountains, home to the Apadana Palace built by Darius I.
question.clue: In this home of a hundred-columned throne room, the Gate of All Nations led to the apadana palace.

swap.leadin: One member of this dynasty made Philip the Arab surrender to him.
swap.text: Name this dynasty which fought the White Huns, and sponsored Zurvan Zoroastrianism. Under Khosrau I, many reforms were enacted, while under Khosrau II, the dynasty reached it territorial zenith, eventually falling after the Battle of Qadisyyah.
swap.clue: Its last great ruler was deposed by Bahram, but with the help of Emperor Maurice regained the throne.

question.leadin: A ruler with this name had the Lakhmid king Al Nu'man III executed.
question.text: Give this name of a Sassanid shahanshah who then annexed the Lakhmid kingdom. An earlier shahanshah of this name went to war with Justinian after his allies raided the Lakhmids, who were then Sassanid vassals.
question.answerHtml: Khosrau [accept Khosrau I, Khosrau II, Khosrau Anushirawan, Khosrau the Just, or Chosroes]
question.clue: The second Sassanid ruler with this name held a truce with the Byzantine Empire because of his friendship with the Emperor Maurice, which lasted until Maurice was killed. The first began an "Eternal Peace" because of a bribe from Justinian, which lasted until that ruler got bored.

swap.text: A university at Gondishapur that was established by this Persian dynasty contained an advanced hospital that gave accreditation to local physicians. This dynasty was founded by Ardashir and included rulers like Shapur.
swap.answerHtml: Sassanian dynasty [or Sassanid Empire; accept the House of Sasan]
swap.clue: This last pre-Islamic Persian dynasty, which unsuccessfully besieged Constantinople in 626.

question.leadin: Heleen Sancisi-Weerdenburg argued that historians relied exclusively on Greek sources on this empire and that there was no solid evidence of its actual existence.
question.text: Name these people who, according to Herodotus, built the capital of Ecbatana and were last ruled by Astyages before his Persian grandson overthrew him around 550 BC.
question.clue: Early kings of these people included Deioces and Phraortes.

swap.leadin: A widely rejected theory links the language of this ancient kingdom to South India's Dravidian language family.
swap.text: Name this kingdom in modern Western Iran whose king, Shutruk-Nahhunte, took the stelae ("STEE-lee") of the Babylonian kings Naram-Sin and Hammurabi back to his capital of Susa during a 12th-century BC invasion of the Kassite Dynasty.
swap.clue: The "Lament for Ur" describes a conquest by these people, whose Shutrukid dynasty later defeated the Kassites and looted the stele bearing the Code of Hammurabi from Babylon.

question.text: Darius' rise to power is described in the Bisitun inscription, which claims that Gaumata, one of these people, pretended to be Smerdis, the brother of Cambyses II. These people, who in Sasanian times were led by a chief figure called the mowbed, are described by Herodotus as one of six Median tribes.
question.clue: Important to both the Medes and Persians were this priestly class which accomplished feats of prophecy, dream-interpretation, and sorcery later named for them.

swap.text: This Sassanid city was the site of an A.D. 363 battle that took place between Shapur II and Emperor Julian, which saw a tactical victory for the Romans. It was the primary capital for both the Parthian and Sassanid Empires.
swap.clue: This city was known by Arabs as "al- Mada'in" or "the cities" due to its many suburbs, one of which was sarcastically dubbed "better than Antioch," while another was home to the patriarch of the Nestorian church.

question.leadin: Its capital was known as Ecbatana to the Greeks, and was probably founded by Cyaxeres.
question.text: Name this empire, whose last ruler Astyages was overtrown by Cyrus the Great.
question.clue: The city of Nineveh was captured by his successor Cyaxares, who extended this kingdom's borders to the Halys river in Asia Minor.

swap.leadin: A ruler with this name founded and named a city which was the location of an academy that served as the inspiration for Baghdad's House of Wisdom.
swap.text: Give this name of the son of Ardashir I, who captured the Roman emperor Valerian during his campaigns to expand the Sassanid Empire westward.
swap.clue: A king with this name built a namesake city on the road between Estakhr and Ctesiphon.

question.leadin: Little is known about this figure, but according to Plutarch, he was tall, and was very manly despite the "delicacy of his looks and effeminacy of his dress."
question.text: Name this Spahbod who was sent by Orodes II to delay the Romans, but ended up defeating them instead, using horse-archers and camels to resupply the archers.
question.clue: According to Plutarch's Parallel Lives, a commander fighting against this leader had to rescind an attempted charge when he saw that his soldier's "hands were riveted to their shields and their feet nailed through and through to the ground" by arrows.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about the last Himyarite king, Abraha's son Ma'd-Karib.
swap.text: Ma'd Karib was assisted by this Sassanid shahanshah during a later Axumite invasion of Himyar, which saw this monarch's general Vahrez win the Battle of Hadhramaut. Earlier, he concluded the Eternal Peace with Justinian the Great.
swap.clue: This Sasanian emperor who succeeded Kavad I. Most historians believe that Yemen came under Sassanid rule during his reign.
